name: Melanotan I (afamelanotide)
summary: A lab-made analog of the skin-darkening hormone alpha-MSH, approved as an implant for a rare light-sensitivity disorder; unlicensed Melanotan I products are used for tanning.
what_it_is: Afamelanotide, also known as Melanotan I, is a lab-made peptide of 13 amino acids modeled on alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (alpha-MSH). It activates the melanocortin 1 receptor in the skin, which raises production of the dark pigment eumelanin regardless of sun or UV exposure. As the prescription implant Scenesse, it helps adults with erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP), a rare disorder that causes painful reactions to light. Unlicensed products sold as Melanotan I for tanning are untested and unregulated.

evidence.why: Two randomized placebo-controlled trials in 168 patients support its FDA-approved use in EPP; it is not approved for cosmetic tanning, and the unlicensed tanning products have only small early trials and case reports.

status_us.label: FDA-approved implant for a rare light disorder (EPP)
status_us.note: Scenesse was approved in October 2019 to increase pain-free light exposure in adults with EPP and must be implanted by a trained health care professional. It is not approved for tanning; products sold as Melanotan I for that purpose are unlicensed and untested, and afamelanotide is not on FDA's list of substances nominated for pharmacy compounding.

benefits.claim: More pain-free time in direct sunlight for people with EPP: a median of 69.4 versus 40.8 hours over 6 months in a US trial of 94 patients, and 6.0 versus 0.8 hours over 9 months in a European trial of 74
Fewer painful light reactions than placebo (77 versus 146) in the European trial
Better quality of life than placebo in both trials

risks.risk: Implant-site reactions (21% versus 10% on placebo), most often discoloration, and nausea (19% versus 14%)
Darker skin and darkening of existing moles and freckles; new moles were reported in 4% versus 2% on placebo, and the label advises full-body skin exams twice a year
Sore throat, cough, fatigue and dizziness, each in 4% to 7%, slightly more often than with placebo

With unlicensed Melanotan I and II used for tanning: flushing, nausea and tiredness in small trials, plus case reports of enlarging or darkening moles, new atypical moles and melanoma (cause not proven)
Unlicensed products have not been tested for quality, and regulators have raised concerns about contamination and infections from shared needles

avoid_if: History of melanoma or many unusual moles, without a dermatologist's advice
interactions: None well documented (no drug interaction studies have been done)

during: Full-body skin exam twice a year
labs.why: The Scenesse label recommends twice-yearly full-body skin exams to watch existing and new pigmented spots; no blood tests are required.

studies.title: Afamelanotide for Erythropoietic Protoporphyria
studies.people: 168 patients with EPP in two trials (94 in the US, 74 in Europe)
studies.finding: Afamelanotide implants increased pain-free time in direct sunlight and improved quality of life versus placebo; side effects were mostly mild and serious events were not judged drug-related.

studies.title: SCENESSE (afamelanotide) implant prescribing information
studies.people: 244 patients with EPP in placebo-controlled trials (125 on afamelanotide)
studies.finding: Implant-site reactions, nausea, sore throat, cough, fatigue, skin darkening and new moles were more common than with placebo; twice-yearly full-body skin exams are recommended.

studies.title: Risks of unregulated use of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone analogues: A review
studies.people: Case reports of unregulated melanotan users
studies.finding: Unregulated melanotan I and II use was linked in case reports to mole changes, new dysplastic moles and four melanomas; the authors note that cause is not proven and contrast this with the tested, approved afamelanotide.

ask_your_clinician: Do my light-sensitivity symptoms fit EPP, and would Scenesse be an option for me?
How often should my skin and moles be checked?
What are the risks of unlicensed tanning peptides compared with sun protection?

notes_for_editor: The Drugs@FDA label opened is the October 2019 original; later revisions were not checked. The maker's 2025 annual report [2] says US approval covers adults only and that a phase 3 vitiligo trial (CUV105) finished recruiting in May 2025. That afamelanotide is Melanotan I ([Nle4-D-Phe7]-alpha-MSH) is stated in a 2012-2013 risk profile hosted by Norway's food safety authority [4] and matches the label's 13-amino-acid sequence; the dermatology review [6] treats unlicensed melanotan products as distinct from the approved drug in quality and testing. The risk profile's line that melanotan is licensed nowhere predates the EU and US approvals and was not used. Trial medians are from the NEJM paper; the label reports slightly different medians from a different analysis.
